scope: Sources used to bound Liminal's Jungian interpretive method, qualitative review process, validation risks, and AI-wellness safety. This registry is not a clinical evidence claim.

preference_order: primary work or authoritative bibliographic record
required_fields: what the source does not support
review_protocol.conflict_rule: Keep credible disagreement in the registry; do not resolve a contested empirical question by deleting the minority source.

sources.citation: Jung, C. G. The Structure and Dynamics of the Psyche, Collected Works, Vol. 8; abstracts hosted by the International Association for Analytical Psychology.
Kiehl, E. The Transcendent Function. International Association for Analytical Psychology.
does_not_support: a universal algorithm for resolving opposites
a license to infer trauma or psychosis

sources.citation: Zaphiriou-Zarifi, H. Amplification. International Association for Analytical Psychology.
does_not_support: fixed universal meanings for every image

sources.citation: Forer, B. R. (1949). The fallacy of personal validation; a classroom demonstration of gullibility. Journal of Abnormal Psychology, 44(1), 118-123. doi:10.1037/h0059240.
does_not_support: the claim that every personally resonant interpretation is false

sources.citation: Lilienfeld, S. O., Wood, J. M., & Garb, H. N. (2000). The Scientific Status of Projective Techniques. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 1(2), 27-66. doi:10.1111/1529-1006.002.
does_not_support: a direct validation study of tarot
the claim that all projective indexes are invalid
the claim that symbolic reflection has no experiential value

sources.citation: Hibbard, S. (2003). A critique of Lilienfeld et al.'s (2000) The Scientific Status of Projective Techniques. Journal of Personality Assessment, 80(3), 260-271. doi:10.1207/S15327752JPA8003_05.
does_not_support: automatic transfer of Rorschach or TAT findings to tarot
removal of the conservative product boundary

sources.citation: O'Brien, B. C., Harris, I. B., Beckman, T. J., Reed, D. A., & Cook, D. A. (2014). Standards for Reporting Qualitative Research: A Synthesis of Recommendations. Academic Medicine, 89(9), 1245-1251. doi:10.1097/ACM.0000000000000388.
does_not_support: using SRQR as a score of methodological validity
the truth of any particular psychological interpretation

sources.citation: Tong, A., Sainsbury, P., & Craig, J. (2007). Consolidated criteria for reporting qualitative research (COREQ): a 32-item checklist for interviews and focus groups. International Journal for Quality in Health Care, 19(6), 349-357. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzm042.
does_not_support: application beyond interviews and focus groups without adaptation
the validity of model-generated psychological conclusions

sources.citation: O'Connor, C., & Joffe, H. (2020). Intercoder Reliability in Qualitative Research: Debates and Practical Guidelines. International Journal of Qualitative Methods, 19, 1-13. doi:10.1177/1609406919899220.
does_not_support: mandatory quantified agreement for every qualitative paradigm

sources.citation: Braun, V., & Clarke, V. (2021). One size fits all? What counts as quality practice in (reflexive) thematic analysis? Qualitative Research in Psychology, 18(3), 328-352. doi:10.1080/14780887.2020.1769238.
World Health Organization. (2021). Ethics and governance of artificial intelligence for health: WHO guidance. ISBN 978-92-4-002920-0.
does_not_support: classification of Liminal as a medical device
